items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Bugs would give Jack and myself the solos... Jack and I decided to do something about that... After that, Jack and I had solos which we were featured in

ctx.x: Fats was a natural hit everywhere we played. As "Bugs" Hamilton had been with Fats a long time, he was normally the leader of the trumpet section because he had parts that he played when Fats only used a small combo. He would give Jack and myself the solos that he didn't care about playing. Sometimes when his lips were not feeling too strong, Bugs would ask me or Jack to take a solo in numbers that he enjoyed playing.

We enjoyed the solos also, but when Bugs lips felt alright the next night, he would play the solos again. Jack and I decided to do something about that. The next time Bugs asked one of us to take his solo and we knew the reason he wanted us to do it, we told him that we were not going to take them one day and he would take them only when he felt good. After that, Jack and I had solos which we were featured in, in every theatre we played.

These gigs were on a weekly basis and sometimes there would be periods of two or three weeks that Fats did not use a big band, but whenever he did the same musicians were usually available. We had a few days once up state in New York and Fats was suffering with the gout in one foot. His doctor had advised him not to drink any whisky but told him that he could drink a little wine every day. So Fats had a gallon of muscatel in his dressing room every day.
